method: A scan format fixes four counts: active samples per line, active lines, samples in a total line (active plus horizontal blanking) and total lines per frame (active plus vertical blanking). The line rate is the pixel clock divided by the samples per total line and the line period is its reciprocal, so 1080p at 25 Hz gives 74.25 MHz / 2,640 = 28.125 kHz and a 35.556 microsecond line, of which 25.859 microseconds carry the 1,920 active samples and 9.697 microseconds are blanking. The frame rate is the line rate divided by the total lines and the frame period is its reciprocal; an interlaced format carries two fields per frame, so its field rate is twice the frame rate. Fractional-rate systems use the matching integer rate divided by 1.001, which is why 59.94 and 29.97 Hz run at a 74.25/1.001 = 74.1758 MHz clock with 2,200 samples per line. The pixel clock can be overridden with a measured value: the line and frame rates then follow the clock and the page reports the deviation from the format's nominal clock. Blanking is counted per total line only; sync widths, the front and back porch split, tolerances, ancillary data and embedded audio are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser.
